edition.jurisdiction: The universal ICEL English, common to ICEL's eleven member episcopal conferences. This is NOT a national adaptation and is not a witness to any conference's proper texts or adaptations.
edition.notes:
The publisher here is the rightsholder, which is why this edition is the highest
tier of exemplar available for the text it carries: nothing establishes that
these are the promulgated words better than the owner's own copy of them.

Two limits, and both are load-bearing.

AS OF WHEN. An authoritative publisher establishes who says so; it does not
establish when, and each conference implements an emendation on its own date.
These files are the 2010-2012 state. The Missal has been emended since — the
collect conclusions after the Prefect's letter of May 2020, the 2013 insertion of
Saint Joseph into Eucharistic Prayers II-IV, the reigning Pope's name, and a
growing Proper of Saints. One file in this library demonstrates the trap
directly: PresidentialTones.pdf sets the Collect of the First Sunday of Advent
with the conclusion ending "one God, for ever and ever", the reading superseded
after that letter. Collate any text taken from here against the emendations in
force for the territory it is being published for, exactly as a missal witness
would be collated.

EXACTNESS OF THE TEXT LAYER. Every file has a text layer and none of them is
byte-exact. Sung text is syllabified across neumes, ligatures appear as single
glyphs, and at least one glyph pair mis-maps — "attain" extracts as "aHain" in
GoodFriday6.pdf. The layer is a finding aid. Transcription is from the page
images, and the de-syllabification is an editorial transformation that must be
recorded, on a text whose permission demands exactness.
edition.publication: Published by ICEL at https://www.icelweb.org/musicfolder/openmusic.html as 188 separately downloadable PDFs; state retrieved 2026-08-21. The chants themselves carry ICEL's 2010 copyright; the library is a mutable web state and this record fixes what it offered on the day it was read.

passages.context:
The one sentence of terms on ICEL's Music for the Roman Missal page, standing
immediately below the title and above the file list, read on 2026-08-21 from the
retained bytes:

"The following music and texts may be reproduced free of charge in printed form,
for non-commercial purposes, in publications not for sale, by parishes,
dioceses, schools, and religious communities, provided that the copyright
acknowledgment which appears at the foot of each page is included."

RECORDED SO THAT IT IS NOT MISCITED, WHICH IS THE ERROR MOST AVAILABLE HERE.
This is the generous-sounding grant and it is the wrong one to lean on. It is
bounded twice over: to PRINTED form, and to a named class of user -- parishes,
dioceses, schools, religious communities -- which this project is not in and must
not describe itself as. It authorises reading and printing these files; it does
not authorise republishing the PDFs, and it is not the basis on which ICEL text
appears on this project's pages.

That basis is the separate Global Computer Networks clause in ICEL's Publication
Policies, artifact page 26, which permits reproducing approved, recognised and
promulgated ICEL texts on a free non-commercial website without written or oral
permission, subject to six conditions. Cite that clause for the text. Cite this
sentence only for what it is: the delivery terms of these particular files.

The two do agree on one point, and it is the point condition (2) turns on: the
copyright acknowledgment at the foot of each page must be included. On these
files that acknowledgment reads "The English translation and chants of The Roman
Missal (c) 2010, International Commission on English in the Liturgy Corporation.
All rights reserved."

work.description: The chanted texts of the Roman Missal, third typical edition, set to music by ICEL and published free by ICEL on its own site. It is a distinct publication and not the Missal: the notice ICEL prints on every page of it claims "the English translation AND CHANTS of The Roman Missal", so the melodies are ICEL's composition standing beside ICEL's translation. Its contents are the sung Order of Mass, every Preface of the Missal including those of the Eucharistic Prayers for Reconciliation and for Various Needs, Eucharistic Prayers I to IV with the proper Communicantes and Hanc igitur, the ritual chants of Holy Week including all ten Good Friday Solemn Intercessions and both forms of the Exsultet, the presidential and reading tones, and organ accompaniments to the principal chants. Registered because it is the rightsholder's own copy of a large part of the Missal's English, and nothing establishes exactness better than that.
